# Introduction 

The TMF658 Loyalty Management API delivers an interface for the management of Loyalty Programs

## API Standard coverage of Functional Framework

This API provides an interface standard for the management of customer loyalty functions as defined in the Functional Framework (GB1033 Functional Framework Guidebook) with specific reference to 3.8.1 (Customer Loyalty and Retention) at sub-domain level 1.

The main use case is to achieve an API-first approach to end-to-end Loyalty Program Management by:

1. Defining a loyalty management library of reusable resources such as:

    1. Event types/topics recognised for rewards processing.
    2. Conditions in the form of reusable expressions applied to qualifying event types.
    3. Actions resulting from qualifying events in terms of program rule definitions.

2. Defining Loyalty Program Product Specifications as a collection of rules where a rule is comprised of qualifying events, conditions and actions.

## Fundamentals

The TMF658 API relies on the asynchronous event pattern. This means that any loyalty program product specification must include one or more PolicyEvent resources that define subscription events/topics in an event-driven ecosystem that represent qualifying events for rewards processing. This implies that the underlying Loyalty Engine will implement event subscriptions in accordance with the LoyaltyProgramProductSpecification PolicyEvent specifications and that these events will be subjected to Loyalty Program Policy Rules.

## Dependencies

In addition, the Loyalty API supports referencing of Policy Rules as defined by TMF723 (Policy Management). A Policy Rule binds events to conditions and, ultimately, resulting actions when events processed meet the policy conditions. In the case of Loyalty Program rules, the actions take the form of behavioural rewards such a points / virtual currency rewards, order creation, offer recommendations, voucher issuing or other forms of businessi interactions. It is important for adopters of TMF658 to understand the Policy Management API as the correct operation of the Loyalty Management functions underpinning it relies on the implementation of Loyalty Rules using the rule definitions managed using TMF723.

The TMF658 API supports the following Loyalty Management business functions:

## Loyalty Programme Management Support

### Program Specification The API supports agility through continuous extensions to overall Loyalty Programs with the management of multiple LoyaltyProgramProductSpecification resources, each with its bound

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

events/topics and associated Loyalty Program policies defining rewarding business rules. It is envisaged that, with adoption of TMF658, Loyalty Programs can be continuously extended to ensure that the programs aids in objectives such as customer behavioural change programs, retention and customer value proposional improvements.

### Member onboarding

Program members are onboarded using the LoyaltyProgramMember resource which is modelled as a specialisation of TMF669 PartyRole. Enrolment is therefore by definition a LoyaltyProgramMember subscribed to a LoyaltyProgramProductSpecification and with an associated LoyaltyAccount to which rewards are accrued to rewards earnings buckets and balances.

### Loyalty Account Management

Loyalty Account is a specialization of the Account schema and is provided as a managed entity of TMF658. This enables specifications of accounts that may be dedicated for a Program Member or may be shared between members. Loyalty Rewards points / virtual currency accrual can therefore be shared by multiple members (e.g. Corporate Programs where employees may utilise from a rewards resource pool) or be a dedicated account per member.

### Program onboarding

Customers may be enrolled to one or more LoyaltyProgramProductSpecification to entitle customers to the benefits associated with the Loyalty Program.

### Benefit Partner Management

Program Benefit Partners may be formally managed as part of Loyalty Programs. Benefit partners can therefore be managed, inclusive of partner benefit catalogues that may be used as part of rewards actions as defined by the TMF723 Policy Management policy definitions.

### Loyalty Earn operations

In certain cases, loyalty programs may allow the consumption of a direct earn operation as opposed to event-policy-action driven rewarding based on emitted operational events. Examples of the use of direct Loyalty Earn operations are:

- Partners with authorization to post directly Loyalty Earn events when customers interact with their brand
- Simple Loyalty Programs that do not require a policy engine to determine earnings
- Extarnal policy/pricing engines determining loyalty rewards actions and use the loyaltyEarn operation to record externally determined rewards in the form of virtual currency / points.

### Direct Loyalty Burn interfaces

The TMF658 loyaltyBurn interface is used by authorized API consumers as part of e- commerce purchase journeys. Loyalty Rewards can therefore be used as payment

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

instrument for partial or full payment during online or other digitally integrated purchase journeys.

### Loyalty Exection Points

The LoyaltyExectionPoint resource represents a rewardable or rewarded point of brand interaction by a Loyalty Program member with the organization running the Loyalty Program. It is an implicit requirement of an underpinning Loyalty Engine to generate accounting records of all Loyalty Points / Virtual Currency earnings and burn transactions. The LoyaltyExecutionPoint resources are retrievable with a GET loyaltyExecutionPoint operations to enable Loyalty Applications to retrieve earnings accrual and usage (burn) records as part of Loyalty Program Management user experience.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

# Use Cases 

## Introduction

The use cases listed in this section illustrates a variety of uses of the TMF658 API to achieve different Loyalty Program objectives. The examples used throughout this specification are structured to illustrated the first two use cases described below.

## Use Case 1 – Rewarding Citizens in a Smart City for use of clean inner-city transportation

The City of Nice identified a rewards use case as part of the Connected Citizen Catalyst project. In this use case, it identified rewarding citizens that park their cars in the various car parks at the edge of the inner city and use green inner-city transportation, e.g the Velo Bleu bicycle transportation system.

The city identified the establishment of a Smart City coalition blockchain and that citizens will be rewarded with a private-ledger cryptocurrency that could then be used to pay for city services and be exchanged for benefits at cities forming part of the Smart City coalition.

The Rewards Program goal is therefore to increase the use of green inner-city transportation with the benefits of reducing noise pollution, increase quality of inner-city life and to reduce pollution.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Use Case 2 - Prepaid subscriber behavioural changes to preserve network capacity

A predominantly prepaid market Mobile Network Operator has determined that their network is overloaded with peak voucher recharge and other top-up mechanisms placing strain on the IN SDP nodes where balance is retained. It was found that peak traffic places high demand on the Account Balance Management Function in the network between 18h00 and 20h00 each weekday.The planning teams were faced with either expanding the ABMF (IN SDP) infrastructure as a costly exercise but worked with Marketing and Customer Retention teams and decided to rather create an incentive program using the TMF658-based Loyalty Engine to move the peak balance top-up load through this program. The Loyalty Program was extended to reward the first 10,000 customers (configurable) recharging from 06h00 to 08h00 each weekday with surprise and delight free data and SMS offers.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Use Case 3 - Loyalty Rewards for optimal refuse removal

The City of Saint Quentin identified a loyalty program use case in which citizens are incentivised to place bins in the street when full instead of scheduled refuse collection days and where IoT events are triggered to report bin placement and bin removal.

This use case is supported with intelligent route planning for refuse removal and with the aim of minimising the periods that bins appear on pavements and therefore contributes to improving the aesthetics of the town.

Citizens are incentivised to remove the bins from the pavement as soon after refuse

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

collection was done. This program is therefore implemented with three rewardable events triggered from IoT devices as follows:

1. A bin placement event - an IoT event is emitted if the citizen places the bin at a measured location
2. A bin volume event - an IoT event is emitted with a refuse volume measurement
3. A bin removal event - an IoT event is emitted when a bin removal event takes place

## Use Case 4 – E-commerce integration as part of purchase journeys

The LoyaltyBurn API resource is a form of payment that can be incorporated as part of customer online purchase journeys for partial or full payment for services and goods using loyalty currency (virtual or monetary). This capability will typically be used by the Loyalty Program owner organisation for purchases by its own customer base, but could also be extended to benefit and other partners to enable Loyalty Program Members to use loyalty earnings towards payment for loyalty program partner products and services.

## Use Case 5 – Direct earning integration using the LoyaltyEarn API operation

While the API standard is primarily designed to support a rules and policy engine approach that processes event streams for rewarding, API consumers with access to the LoyaltyEarn API operation can use this interface to honour agreements for direct loyalty earnings.

The API consumers using this operation will typically be trusted internal systems or benefit Partners with which explicit earnings agreements exist.

## Use Case 6 – Managing a diversity of rewards benefit types

For qualifying events received by an underlying Loyalty Engine based on the TMF658 resource model, a variety of Loyalty Action types can result from qualifying events. These are as follows:

- **LoyaltyEarn**: The action resulting from a qualifying event is that the customer earns loyalty points/ virtual currency.
- **LoyaltyBurn**: The action resulting from a qualifying event is that the customer loyalty points/virtual currency balance is reduced.
- **CustomerOrder**: An order is placed on behalf of the Loyalty Program Member
- **BusinessInteraction**: This action type represents a specific business interaction that could be a fulfilment operation with a benefit partner. These interactions could be simple, atomic transactions or could be orchestrated, multi-step events involved to fulfil the intended benefit.
- **VoucherIssue**: A voucher is issued to the Loyalty Program Member for use.
- **Offer**: An offer is created and communicated with the Loyalty
- **TierChange**: The qualifying event results in a Loyalty Program tier update within a Tiered loyalty program context.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

# Support of polymorphism and extension patterns

Support of polymorphic collections and types and schema based extension is provided by means of a list of generic meta-attributes that we describe below. Polymorphism in collections occurs when entities inherit from base entities, for instance a BillingAccount and SettlementAccount inheriting properties from the abstract Account entity.

Generic support of polymorphism and pattern extensions is described in the TMF API Guidelines v3.0 Part 2 document.

The @type attribute provides a way to represent the actual class type of an entity. For example, within a list of Account instances some may be instances of LoyaltyAccount where other could be instances of FinancialAccount. The @type gives this information. All resources and sub-resources of this API have a @type attributes that can be provided when this is useful.

The @referredType can be used within reference entities (like for instance an AccountRef object) to explicitly denote the actual entity type of the referred class. Notice that in reference entities the @type, when used, denotes the class type of the reference itself, such as LoyaltyAccountRef or FinancialAccountRef, and not the class type of the referred object. However since reference classes are rarely sub-classed, @type is generally not useful in reference objects.

The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined properties of an Entity or to specify the expected _characteristics_ of an entity.

The @baseType attribute gives a way to provide explicitly the base of class of a given resource that has been extended.

## RESOURCE MODEL 

### Managed Entity and Task Resource Models

### LoyaltyProgramProductSpecification resource

The loyalty program product specification resource is the root entity for product specification management. A loyalty program product specification is a detailed description of a loyalty program made available externally in the form of a LoyaltyProduct to LoyaltyProgramMembers. LoyaltyProgramProductSpecification defines one or more Loyalty Rules (PolicyRule resource) that must be checked to identify the actions to apply.

### LoyaltyAccount resource

A LoyaltyAccount corresponds to a set of balances to carry loyalty movement according to different validity period and unit. The LoyaltyAccount is a container for one of more LoyaltyBalances. A LoyaltyAccount may be required to realize a LoyaltyProgramProduct according to the rules carried by the corresponding LoyaltyProgramProductSpecification. A LoyaltyAccount may collect results from one or more LoyaltyProgramProduct resources.

Anaccount receivable aggregates the amounts of one or more partyaccounts (billing or settlement) owned by a given party. |

### LoyaltyExecutionPoint resource

A LoyaltyExecutionPoint is a type of Policy Execution Point. A LoyaltyExecutionPoint tracks the application of a Loyalty Policy Action and serves as a record of an applied Loyalty Policy Action.

# API OPERATIONS 

Remember the following Uniform Contract:

| Operation on Entities | Uniform API Operation | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Query Entities | GET Resource | GET must be used to retrieve arepresentation of a resource. |
| Create Entity | POST Resource | POST must be used to create anew resource |
| Partial Update of an Entity | PATCH Resource | PATCH must be used to partiallyupdate a resource |
| Complete Update of an Entity | PUT Resource | PUT must be used tocompletely update a resourceidentified by its resource URI |
| Remove an Entity | DELETE Resource | DELETE must be used toremove a resource |
| Execute an Action on an Entity | POST on TASK Resource | POST must be used to executeTask Resources |
| Other Request Methods | POST on TASK Resource | GET and POST must not beused to tunnel other requestmethods. |

Filtering and attribute selection rules are described in the TMF REST Design Guidelines.

Notifications are also described in a subsequent section.

This operation allows partial updates of a LoyaltyProgramProductSpecification entity. Support of json/merge ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ([http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub- resource attributes and default value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH operation. Hence these tables are not repeated here.

Support of json/merge ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ([http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub- resource attributes and default value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH operation. ```

**Description**

This operation allows partial updates of a LoyaltyAccount entity. Support of json/merge ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ([http://tools.ietf.org/](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) [html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub-resource attributes and default value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH operation. Hence these tables are not repeated here.

# API NOTIFICATIONS 

For every single of operation on the entities use the following templates and provide sample REST notification POST calls.

It is assumed that the Pub/Sub uses the Register and UnRegister mechanisms described in the REST Guidelines reproduced below.

## Register listener

**POST /hub**

**Description**

Sets the communication endpoint address the service instance must use to deliver information about its health state, execution state, failures and metrics. Subsequent POST calls will be rejected by the service if it does not support multiple listeners. In this case DELETE /api/hub/{id} must be called before an endpoint can be created again.

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 409 if request is not successful.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a request for registering a listener.

**Request**

```
POST /api/hub
Accept: application/json
{
    "callback": "http://in.listener.com"
}
```

**Response**

```
Content-Type: application/json
Location: /api/hub/42
{
    "id":"42",
    "callback": "http://in.listener.com",    "query":""
}
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Unregister listener

**DELETE /hub/{id}**

**Description**

Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub..

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 404 if the resource is not found.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a request for un-registering a listener.

**Request**

```
DELETE /api/hub/42
Accept: application/json
```

**Response**

```
204
```

## Publish Event to listener

**POST /client/listener**

**Description**

Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub.

Provides to a registered listener the description of the event that was raised. The /client/listener url is the callback url passed when registering the listener.

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 201 if the service is able to set the configuration.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a notification received by the listener. In this example “EVENT TYPE” should be replaced by one of the notification types supported by this API (see Notification resources Models section) and EVENT BODY refers to the data structure of the given notification type.

**Request**

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

```
POST /client/listener
Accept: application/json
{
    "event": {
        EVENT BODY    },
    "eventType": "EVENT_TYPE"
}
```

**Response**

```
201
```

For detailed examples on the general TM Forum notification mechanism, see the TMF REST Design Guidelines.
